summary: Alessandro Graheli is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022), and at the University of Toronto (attested 2026).

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford (BA) and SOAS (MA), and completed his doctorate under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson. His posts include Harvard, Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2006), and Ashoka University (attested 2020).

Alex Wayman (1921–2004) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at UCLA and UC Berkeley (PhD), where he was supervised by Ferdinand Lessing. He taught at Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1966) and served on the faculty at Columbia University (1967–1991).

Alexander Berzin (born 1944) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard (PhD), studying under Masatoshi Nagatomi. From ~1972 to 1998, he was a founding member of the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Alexander C. McKay (born 1953) is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alexander Coburn Soper (1904–1993) worked in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Hamilton College and Princeton University (PhD, 1944). He taught at Bryn Mawr College, served as a professor at New York University (1960), and edited Artibus Asiae (1958–1993).

Alexander Cunningham (1814–1893) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and under James Prinsep. He founded the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director (1861–1865) and later as director-general (1871–1885).
Alexander Duff (1806–1878) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He was educated at the University of St Andrews (~1821–1829) and the University of Aberdeen.
Alexander Freiman studied under Christian Bartholomae (~1906–1907) and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.

Alexander Gardner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under the supervision of Donald S. Lopez Jr., and he held a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Alexander Hamilton (1762–1824) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit (appointed 1806) and Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature (appointed 1808) at the East India Company College.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. A PhD candidate at the University of Toronto, he has served as a research fellow at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston (1775–1849) studied law at the University of Göttingen (~1792–1795) and Lincoln's Inn (~1795–1799). He served as chief justice on the Executive Council of Ceylon (~1811–1819) and founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Alexander Kabanoff (1952–2000) was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2000, he was a Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek (1802–1870) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1826–1849) and Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1849–1870).

Alexander Lubotsky (born 1956) is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University (PhD under Robert S. P. Beekes), where he became full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics in 1999.
Alexander Macmillan works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at SIT Graduate Institute, where he was advised by Elizabeth Morrison (attested 2013).
Alexander Murray (1775–1813) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at the University of Edinburgh (~1794–1806) and later held a post there from ~1812 to 1813.

Alexander Ong Hsu specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2017) under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and later held a teaching position at North Dakota State University.

Alexander Piatigorsky (1929–2009) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. After studying at Moscow State University, he worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1957–1968) and later served as Professor of the Ancient History of South Asia at SOAS (1990–2001).
